brief: What we look for when hiring engineers in 2026 (it's not coding tests).

slots.author: Sarah Chen
slots.headline: How We Hire Engineers in 2026
slots.body: Coding tests are out. Here's what top engineering teams actually look for when hiring elite talent this year.

slots.author: Sarah Chen
slots.title: Systems Thinking First
slots.body: We give messy real-world scenarios and watch how candidates decompose complexity before writing a single line.

slots.author: Sarah Chen
slots.title: Collaboration Over Speed
slots.body: The best engineers ask questions early. We pair program on unfamiliar codebases to see communication in action.

slots.author: Sarah Chen
slots.title: Learn in Real Time
slots.body: Tech changes fast. We care more about how you navigate docs, debug unknown stacks, and adapt on the fly.

slots.author: Sarah Chen
slots.title: Own the Outcome
slots.body: We look for engineers who chase root causes, not ticket closures. Do you fix the bug or the system?

slots.author: Sarah Chen
slots.title: User Empathy Matters
slots.body: Great code solves human problems. We ask candidates to explain who benefits and why the feature exists.

slots.author: Sarah Chen
slots.title: Build the Future
slots.body: The 2026 engineering interview is a conversation, not an exam. Ready to rethink your hiring process?
